marks.gloss_en: השתא מיפרק לא פרקינן עלויה, משחט שחטינן עלויה? -- if consecrated animals are not even redeemed for a temporary blemish, surely a firstborn is not slaughtered for it
דתניא: ... יכול יפדו על מום עובר? תלמוד לומר אשר לא יקריבו ממנה -- the source of the KV's premise (kind tanya_kevatei for דתניא, under protest)
מום עובר סברא הוא: השתא מיפרק לא פרקינן עלויה, משחט שחטינן עלויה? (= p_mum_over_sevara, kv_mum_over)
[the exclusion of] a temporary blemish is from reasoning
בעינא מום רע, וליכא (= p_baeina_mum_ra)
אי הכי, מום עובר נמי! אלמה תנן: ולא מן העור? -- if 'any' amplifies, a temporary blemish too; yet the mishna excludes damage to the skin
I require an 'ILL blemish', and [in a hidden blemish] there is none
איבעית אימא: אם כן פסח ועור למה לי? -- if so, why do I need lame and blind?
might they be redeemed for a temporary blemish? Scripture says: 'of which they may not bring an offering to the Lord'
כעדשה -- אין, בציר מכעדשה -- לא? ורמינהו: RYbRY himself validates a needle for piercing, and the Chachamim say the piercing blemishes a kohen -- so a needle-hole, smaller than a lentil, is a blemish
לא קשיא -- כאן לשחוט, כאן לפסול (= p_kan_lishchot_kan_lifsol)
Rav Chana bar Ketina: here [the lentil] is for slaughtering [the firstborn on its account]; there [any hole] is for disqualifying

אם כן, עשיתה דברי בית שמאי ודברי בית הלל אחד! דתנן: the man-made window is as the large drill, which is as a Neronian sela -- so BS's drill and BH's sela are one measure. (Rav Pappa's answer at 38a.16 is reified as p_pappa_makdeach_gadol and falls to two unanswered objections; it is not listed here.)
the mishna: a window not made by man -- its measure is a large fist, the fist of Ben Avatiach
the first tanna: the hole in the ear [that is a blemish] is the size of a karshina
a tanna taught: their words are close to being equal
R' Yosei b'R' Yehuda: 'and you shall take' (Deut 15:17) -- anything taken by hand, including a thorn, a needle, a gimlet and a stylus, is valid for piercing the slave's ear
Yudan beRabbi expounded: when they pierce, they pierce only in the earlobe
the Chachamim: a Hebrew slave who is a kohen is not pierced, because he becomes blemished
Rav Sherevya: karshina is hinda (bitter vetch)
(queried) the measure is a karshina that enters and leaves the hole
Beit Shammai: a spine lacking two vertebrae does not impart tent-impurity
Shmuel: [Beit Hillel's] 'enough that, removed from a living man, he dies' is the size of a sela
Rav Safra: [Rav Tachlifa] told him an amoraic tradition
the mishna: a man-made window -- they measured it as the large drill of the chamber
the mishna: [the firstborn's ear] was split, even though it lacks nothing -- [a blemish for which it is slaughtered]
rather: a split and a nick -- whether by the hand of Heaven or by human hand
